article.headline: Scores from last Night: Ripley rallies in overtime; Pontotoc ends Louisville’s unbeaten start
article.html:
Ripley’s girls turned a difficult opening half into an overtime victory at Mooreville, and the Tigers’ boys completed a tight basketball sweep. Pontotoc’s girls delivered another notable result Tuesday, November 17, handing Louisville its first reported loss in a 59-53 home win.

Across this selection of Mississippi varsity finals, Harrison Central, Tylertown, Center Hill, Meridian and West Union preserved unbeaten basketball records. Oak Grove’s boys soccer team also stayed unbeaten while ending Gulfport’s loss-free opening.

Ripley’s girls complete the comeback; boys win narrowly

Ripley’s 67-62 girls basketball win at Mooreville required an extended recovery. The Troopers won the first quarter 23-8 and the second 17-11, but Ripley reversed the scoring pattern after the break, taking the third 18-8 and the fourth 21-10. The Tigers then outscored Mooreville 9-4 in overtime. The completed game page lists Ripley at 3-1 and Mooreville at 3-3.

The boys game was another narrow Ripley win, 61-59 on the road. The Tigers’ listed record improved to 3-0, while Mooreville fell to 4-2. Together, the results gave Ripley both varsity games without the cushion of a comfortable final margin.

Pontotoc hands Louisville its first loss and takes both games

Pontotoc’s girls beat Louisville 59-53 to reach a listed 3-1 record. Louisville is now listed at 6-1, ending the Wildcats’ unbeaten opening. The Warriors earned their third listed victory while stopping a Louisville team that had won its first six reported games.

Pontotoc’s boys won 68-34 against Louisville, completing the basketball sweep with a much wider margin. The Warriors are listed at 2-1 and the Wildcats at 1-6 after the nonconference game.

Harrison Central and Tylertown win unbeaten matchups

Harrison Central’s girls won 44-14 at St. Patrick and moved to a listed 4-0. St. Patrick is listed at 6-1. The Red Rebels separated themselves defensively: the posted box score gives the Fighting Irish no points in the second quarter, six in the third and three in the fourth. Harrison Central’s 16-6 third quarter extended the advantage after halftime.

Tylertown’s boys defeated visiting Amite County 59-38. The Chiefs are listed at 4-0, while the Trojans took their first reported defeat and are now 4-1. Those results settled the unbeaten matchups highlighted in Tuesday’s Games To Watch preview.

More unbeaten boys teams keep winning

Center Hill beat Lewisburg 69-59 in an all-DeSoto County boys matchup, leaving the Mustangs at a listed 4-0 and the Patriots at 2-2. Meridian also stayed perfect, winning 73-56 at Neshoba Central to reach 5-0. Center Hill protected its unbeaten start at home, while Meridian kept winning on the road.

West Union won 82-65 at East Union and is listed at 5-0, with East Union at 1-2. The Eagles added another road victory to their perfect opening, while the Urchins took their second listed defeat.

North Pontotoc sweeps; Corinth and Kossuth girls win

North Pontotoc swept its basketball visit to Alcorn Central. The boys won 31-26, with a 12-4 third quarter providing the Vikings’ clearest scoring advantage after closely matched opening periods. The completed listing puts North Pontotoc at 5-1. The girls won 43-35 and are listed at 5-2.

Elsewhere in girls basketball, Corinth won 58-24 at Red Bay, Alabama, reaching a listed 4-1. Kossuth beat visiting Marshall Academy 59-32 to move to 3-2. The Aggies’ result came at home; Corinth earned its win across the state line.

Soccer: Oak Grove stays unbeaten; Booneville posts a shutout

Oak Grove’s boys won 3-0 at Gulfport, keeping their unbeaten record intact at a listed 7-0-2. The Admirals are listed at 5-1-1 after their first reported loss. Gulfport won the girls match, 3-1 against Oak Grove, so the schools split the varsity soccer results.

Booneville’s boys beat Lafayette 3-0 on the road to reach a listed 5-0. The Blue Devils scored twice before halftime and once afterward, according to the box score, while keeping Lafayette off the scoreboard. The Commodores are listed at 1-4.

Pontotoc paired its basketball success with a soccer sweep of Grenada: the boys won 6-0 and the girls won 7-0. The completed pages list the Warriors’ boys at 3-2 and girls at 4-1. Neither Grenada varsity team scored in the reported matches.

Oxford wins in Lewisburg; boys need a shootout

Oxford’s girls won 2-1 at Lewisburg in a match whose scoring all came after halftime. The Chargers are listed at 4-1 and the Patriots at 4-2. The box score records a scoreless first half, followed by Oxford’s two goals and Lewisburg’s one.

The boys match finished level at 1-1 before Oxford won the shootout 4-3. Lewisburg scored in the first half and Oxford in the second, then the Chargers took the shootout. The shootout tally is separate from the match’s goal score; it should not be read as a 4-3 regulation result.
